question: How do I pray using the Lord's Prayer as a model?
answer: Pray it slowly, line by line, adding your own words. It begins with relationship ("Our Father in heaven"), puts God's name, kingdom and will first, then brings daily needs ("Give us today the bread we need"), confession and forgiveness, and a request for protection from the evil one (Matthew 6:9–13). It is both a prayer to pray as it stands and a frame for our own prayers.

question: How can I tell if an impression in prayer is from God?
answer: Treat impressions with openness and care: "Test everything; keep hold of what is good" (1 Thessalonians 5:21). Weigh them against Scripture, since God never contradicts His written Word; against conscience; against the counsel of mature believers; and by the fruit they bear over time. God speaks above all through the Bible, so knowing what He has already said is the best way to recognise His voice.

question: Why does God not answer some prayers?
answer: Sometimes God says "wait," and as Andrew Murray wrote, we must "learn to give God time." Sometimes He says "no" because He has something better, as Paul learned when the Lord told him, "My grace is enough for you" (2 Corinthians 12:9). Even when we do not know why, we hold on to God's goodness: "whenever we ask for something in line with His will, He listens to us" (1 John 5:14). Unanswered prayer is not unheard prayer.
